quarterly_data.signal: CFO Judith Hartmann: net sales increased by 3% (currency and portfolio adjusted) to EUR 24.3 billion in the first six months; in Q2 sales increased by 2% to EUR 10.9 billion. EBITDA before special items rose 7% to EUR 6.6 billion in the first half, including an increase of 2% to EUR 2.1 billion in Q2. Core EPS was EUR 3.66 for the first six months (up 3%, CEO); Q2 core EPS of EUR 0.95 was 17% below prior year, given non-recurring benefits in taxes and the reconciliation results in 2025. Foreign exchange effects were not a material headwind this quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 sales EUR 24.3 billion (+3%); Q2 sales EUR 10.9 billion (+2%); H1 EBITDA bsi EUR 6.6 billion (+7%); Q2 EBITDA bsi EUR 2.1 billion (+2%); H1 core EPS EUR 3.66 (+3%); Q2 core EPS EUR 0.95 (-17%)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Bill Anderson on first-half divisions: Crop Science sales grew 5.5%, driven by seeds and traits including additional licensing revenue posted in Q1, with EBITDA margin expanded to 31%. Pharmaceuticals sales remained flat, with NUBEQA and KERENDIA combining to grow 66%, overcoming significant and expected declines in Xarelto; Eylea is down 27% on biosimilar pressure, with the eight-milligram business now half of Eylea sales; the base business is growing in part due to strong volume growth in radiology; Pharma EBITDA margin is 26%, in line with expectations as investment in future growth continues in the second half. Consumer Health grew 3.5%, with particularly strong growth in nutritionals and dermatology; its EBITDA margin is trailing prior year but on track to meet the outlook.
quarterly_data.figure: Crop Science +5.5%, margin 31%; Pharma flat, NUBEQA+KERENDIA +66%, Eylea -27%, margin 26%; Consumer Health +3.5%

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Judith Hartmann: first-half free cash flow was negative EUR 2.7 billion versus minus EUR 1.4 billion a year earlier, driven by litigation-related payouts amounting to EUR 2.5 billion in the first half, plus higher incentive payouts in Q2. Net financial debt was EUR 33.6 billion, up EUR 1.1 billion versus the end of Q1, driven by litigation payouts, the Perfuse acquisition and foreign exchange.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 FCF negative EUR 2.7 billion (prior year minus EUR 1.4 billion); litigation payouts EUR 2.5 billion; net financial debt EUR 33.6 billion (+EUR 1.1 billion vs Q1)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Judith Hartmann reiterated the group outlook on sales, earnings and free cash flow at constant currencies for full year 2026, seeing a balanced risk and opportunity profile. Net financial debt is now anticipated at EUR 29 billion-EUR 30 billion, down from previously guided EUR 32 billion-EUR 33 billion, reflecting the minority equity investment by Apollo with closing expected in the second half. The updated FX estimate (June month-end spot rates) leads to a slightly lower headwind to net sales and core EPS than the last estimate. Pharma does not expect tariffs to materially affect the outlook this year, while monitoring MFN drug-pricing policies; Crop Science is monitoring weather, including potential El Nino impacts; Consumer Health watches U.S. consumer sentiment and seasonal categories.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 outlook reiterated at constant currencies; net financial debt EUR 29 billion-EUR 30 billion (was EUR 32 billion-EUR 33 billion)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Bill Anderson: asundexian received priority review in both the U.S. and China, and Bayer is preparing for a planned launch at the end of 2026 or beginning of 2027; in the phase III trial it showed a 26% reduction in second strokes. Management intends to launch in every country possible, including Europe and Germany, while holding pricing conversations to ensure it is appropriately valued.
quarterly_data.figure: asundexian launch end of 2026 or beginning of 2027; 26% reduction in second strokes (phase III)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Bill Anderson on portfolio moves: Bayer closed the acquisition of Perfuse Therapeutics, a novel development medicine in glaucoma and diabetic retinopathy; last month it consolidated its U.S. glyphosate business into Ruvion, a distinct semi-independent entity meant to be nimbler in a commodity-driven market; and it announced a license agreement for broad commercialization of hybrid wheat. He said the glyphosate profit margin is very low, 'approaching zero' at times, one of the lowest-profit products in the portfolio. Bayer is open to deals with Chinese biotech, having done partnerships with Chinese biotech companies and startups.

CEO Bill Anderson on litigation: on June 25th the U.S. Supreme Court ruled in Monsanto v. Durnell that claims grounded in state failure-to-warn theories are preempted, which he called 'a really important step for limiting litigation in the future.' The proposed class settlement is moving ahead; the opt-out period closed on June 4th and the final approval hearing in Missouri state court is scheduled for August 19th, with a final decision expected later this year. On PCBs, Bayer aims to enforce Monsanto's indemnity agreements, with a case moving forward in federal court.
quarterly_data.figure: class settlement final approval hearing August 19th; opt-out period closed June 4th

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Bill Anderson: headcount in Q2 was roughly stable with no fixed job-reduction target under Dynamic Shared Ownership; AI is being incorporated very rapidly in enterprise systems and tools for staff, and he expects Bayer to get leaner and more productive over time. On structure, management keeps an open mind on spin-offs or divestitures but will stay focused on five priorities: the pharma pipeline, containing litigation, de-leveraging, Crop Science profitability and a leaner company. Low water on the Rhine has so far had no impact on Bayer.
